turn_text: This is OPB. I'm Donald Orr. And I'm Tiffany Camhigh. Unless something drastic happens, government funding is set to expire this weekend. The shutdown will mean paychecks to all federal employees, including the military. We'll cease to go out. And some employees will be required to work without pay. Food assistance payments and funding for food and water inspections will also stop. The Senate passed a stopgap funding plan yesterday, but it appears unlikely that it will succeed in the House, where a small group of far-right Republicans are pledging to shut down the government. Here to give us some more context is Congresswoman Lori Chavez-Deremer. She's a Republican who represents Oregon's fifth district, which stretches from Bend to Oregon City. Congresswoman, thanks for joining us.

turn_text: Well, I think the biggest issue is the frustration probably that we're all feeling at this moment. I can't tell you how frustrated I am. I do not want a government shutdown. I think that that is not going to benefit Oregonians or any American who counts on certain things, uncertainty in their everyday lives. So I'm doing everything in my office can. to make sure that we're in conversations in order to avoid just that. We're down to the final days of getting this done. There are a few holdouts who want to massively cut a lot of the appropriations bills. And I can tell you last night on the floor, we had amendments to the agriculture bill and all nine, I did not vote with my party. While we all want to make sure that we're addressing the deficit of $33 trillion and know that we need to make certain cuts across the board, there are certain ones that I cannot stand for and agriculture is one of those.

turn_text: What we're talking about is discretionary spending. Mandatory spending will stay in place. We won't be touching that. But, you know, here's what's important to me. Making sure that my constituents know that I'm fighting for them every single day, whether it be our National Guard, whether it be our TSA, whether it be we're opening up our national parks. People want access. People want to know that we're transparent, that we're fighting for them, that we're actually going to have a conversation about what this looks like. I'm going to work with my colleagues and if it's going to take working with bipartisan colleagues, if it's going to take working within my own party and letting those few, five to seven members of our Republican conference know that I am not going to give up my values of fighting for Oregon and let this government shut down.

turn_text: Well, certainly what we're talking about now is within our own conference, making sure that we can get these appropriations bills now. We will be on the floor this afternoon and tonight. They're debating now on four different appropriations. The rule passed, we heard agriculture last night, we're going to start to hear homeland and some of the others. We're hoping to get those done by Friday and then have a continuing resolution come to the floor within the conference. I've also worked with problem solvers. I am a problem solver. We have the Keep America Open Act and I think that that is a strong piece of legislation. It's bipartisan. It funds the government through January 11th, giving us more time to pass the rest of the appropriations bills at the levels agreed to. in the Bipartisan Fiscal Responsibility Act. That will cut spending by $2.1 trillion over the next six years and it will still keep the government open. It also addresses the crisis that we're seeing every single day at this other border. That is something that, again, it is not a partisan issue. This is an American issue. This is something that people feel very desperately that they want to address. It also provides funding for disaster relief, which we have seen a lot of our states in need, and it includes extenders for critical programs like temporary assistance for needy families and for community health centers. This is a framework that the problem solvers has come up with. So well before we see Senate CR, we're going to do everything we can before that.
